---
title: "Output and figures"
---

## What a cell shows

A cell shows, in order, what it printed and what it displayed, and then —
if its last statement is an expression — the value of that expression, as
a notebook does. A trailing `;` suppresses the value.

```{er2}
sym x
print("printed first")
factor(x^4 - 1)
```

```{er2}
expand((x + 1)^5);
```

## Mathematics

A value with a LaTeX form is shown as display maths. That covers every ER2
type and every SymPy expression; other values are shown as text.

```{er2}
Matrix([[1, x], [x, 1]]).det()
```

```{er2}
GF(9).gen()^4, NumberField(x^2 + 5).class_number()
```

`show()` displays each of its arguments as maths, wherever it is called:

```{er2}
for k in range(1, 4):
    show(diff(sin(x)^k, x))
```

## Inline code

An inline expression in prose is evaluated where it appears. It is shown
as text, or as inline maths when it is `latex(…)`:

````markdown
The derivative of $\sin^3 x$ is `{er2} latex(diff(sin(x)^3, x))`.
````

The derivative of $\sin^3 x$ is `{er2} latex(diff(sin(x)^3, x))`.

## Figures

Every Matplotlib figure left open at the end of a cell is saved and shown,
then closed: SVG for HTML, PDF for LaTeX and PDF output, PNG for everything
else (`fig-format` overrides it). Matplotlib's own return values, such as
the list of lines `plt.plot` returns, are not shown.

```{er2}
#| label: fig-sigma
#| fig-cap: "The sum of divisors, $\\sigma(n)$, with $n$ for comparison."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
ns = range(1, 101)
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3))
plt.bar(ns, [sigma(n) for n in ns])
plt.plot(ns, ns, color="black")
```

@fig-sigma is numbered and cross-referenced like any Quarto figure.

## Caching

`freeze: auto` or `freeze: true` store results in `_freeze/`, and the
paths stored there are relative, so the cache can be committed and
replayed elsewhere. Quarto honours `freeze` only when a whole project is
rendered; `quarto render one-file.qmd` always executes.
